producer_report.summary: Reading acceptance now refuses a code or tests reading that has a behavior criterion but no `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path. The root cause was the reading stage designing seams from a general idea of the feature without surveying the code. I added `check_code_survey` to reading.rs, called from `check_reading_acceptance`. If the reading creates a record or data file under crates/ (or changes a `records.rs`), the survey must also name `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` or a round-trip test; the word allow-list alone is refused. The check reads only assumptions and deliverables, never criterion text, so a criterion saying records/ is untouched triggers nothing. The doc comment and a new CHANGELOG entry say the change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended, which the replay reads as intended. The reader brief gets a fifth rule line and a `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` paragraph. I added 7 unit tests in reading.rs and one in briefs.rs, and raised the rule-section size bound in the existing rule-line test from 1200 to 2400 bytes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a unit test shows that a reading with a create deliverable for a record or data file under crates/ is refused unless the survey names check_record_file, AnyRecord, or a named round-trip test function or path. A survey that only mentions 'allow-list' in passing is refused. A criterion that mentions records/ only to exclude it does not trigger the requirement. Docs-only readings, readings with no capability and readings with only content criteria are still accepted, and the existing reading tests pass unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: The reader brief in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tells the reader to write the 'Code survey:' assumption before giving behavior criteria. The survey covers the entry point and ordering of resolution and probing, the records validation allow-list, and how to measure the property directly. It also tells the reader to write an intended-refusal criterion when a request adds or tightens a refusal rule. The briefs token-budget tests pass under `cargo test -p athena-context`.

mistakes: My first CHANGELOG assertion in code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended failed because the phrase wraps across lines; I fixed it by normalising whitespace.
I put -q after `--` on a clippy command, and clippy rejected it; I reran it with -q before the `--`.
My first draft of the doc comment described what jobs 20261028-055601-hg0n and 20261028-082151-67fa did in detail I had not read. I replaced it with only what the brief states.
learnings: READING_RULES lines are counted by the rule-line test as lines starting '- ' in the section up to the next '\n# ', so the guide paragraph must not start a line with '- '.
The athena-core reading tests use class 'feature' and content criteria, so a gate on class code/tests with a behavior criterion leaves them untouched.
The CHANGELOG wraps lines, so a test that looks for a phrase in it has to normalise whitespace first.
desires: A way to read the saved output of a long test run; the tool-result file was outside the working directory, so I reran with -q.
